text:
julie: Hey support — customer ACME-392 Private (VPC) can no longer pull models or apt packages since last night. Deploys failing with TLS/DNS errors. We see `getaddrinfo: Name or service not known` for model-registry and `curl: (35) SSL_connect error` for models CDN. Can we get an egress allowlist for everything Redwood needs?

matt: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl -v) and a traceroute? Also confirm if they're using a corporate proxy or TLS inspection.

julie: pasted logs from host (redacted):
```
$ curl -v https://model-registry.redwood-inference.com/v1/models
* Rebuilt URL to: https://model-registry.redwood-inference.com/v1/models
*   Trying 10.0.2.5...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect to 10.0.2.5 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to model-registry.redwood-inference.com port 443: Connection timed out
* Closing connection 0
curl: (7) Failed to connect to model-registry.redwood-inference.com port 443: Connection timed out
```
and traceroute: `traceroute to model-registry.redwood-inference.com (10.0.2.5), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets` — it resolves to a private IP in their NAT and drops at their firewall.

The customer says DNS for `packages.redwood-inference.com` also returns NXDOMAIN intermittently. No corporate proxy configured in our agent.

sam: Likely causes: 1) egress blocked by firewall (most common), 2) private DNS overrides / split-horizon returning private IPs, 3) TLS interception (if a proxy is doing MITM you'll see cert errors). Quick checklist: allow outbound TCP/443 to our hostnames, ensure DNS resolution to public IPs, and if you have TLS inspection, either bypass these hostnames or allow cert passthrough.

Here is the minimal allowlist we ask for (recommended: allow FQDNs, SNI-aware allow rules where possible):
- model-registry.redwood-inference.com
- models-cdn.redwood-inference.com
- auth.redwood-inference.com
- packages.redwood-inference.com (apt repos)
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com (metrics/heartbeat)
- model-artifacts.s3.amazonaws.com (object storage fallback)
- registry-1.docker.io (container pulls for some images)
Ports: TCP 443 (primary), TCP 80 (redirects/health), UDP/TCP 53 (DNS) and TCP 853 (DNS-over-TLS) if used.

IPs/CIDRs (for teams that only allow IPs; note these are best-effort and can change):
- 34.123.0.0/16  (models CDN / artifacts)
- 52.210.0.0/16  (registry endpoints)
These are published ranges for our CDN origin and artifact buckets; we recommend allowing FQDNs instead of pinned IPs.

If you inspect TLS (MITM): either 1) add an exception so TLS passthrough is used for the FQDNs above, or 2) allow installation of the customer's MITM CA into our Private agent — but we prefer passthrough.

Example firewall rule we ask customers to add: 
```
ALLOW OUTBOUND tcp any -> (model-registry.redwood-inference.com, models-cdn.redwood-inference.com) ports 443
description: allow redwood model registry & CDN for Private deployment
```

Also: ensure the VPC's resolver returns public A/AAAA for those hostnames. If they have split DNS for `redwood-inference.com`, please share the records.

maya: Thanks, this is clear. Two quick Qs: do you have a single CSV with all FQDNs + ports we can import? And do you want us to add by FQDN or by the example CIDRs? We prefer FQDN + SNI passthrough in our firewall rules.

julie: I'll paste a CSV and a short note for their networking team. Use FQDNs + ports, and ask them to enable SNI passthrough. CSV below:
```
host,port,note
model-registry.redwood-inference.com,443,model metadata and auth
models-cdn.redwood-inference.com,443,model artifacts CDN
auth.redwood-inference.com,443,auth/token endpoints
packages.redwood-inference.com,443,apt repos and yum
telemetry.redwood-inference.com,443,metrics & heartbeat
s3.amazonaws.com,443,artifact fallback
registry-1.docker.io,443,docker pulls
```

deploy-bot: Automated note: customer ACME-392 reported 3 failed model pulls since 2026-03-17T02:10:00Z. Correlation: Private agent outbound blocked errors.

maya: We'll add FQDN rules with SNI passthrough under change request EGRESS-REDWOOD-2026-03. Estimated rollout: 2 hours, will notify once applied. If DNS still resolves to private IPs after this, please open a follow-up with the customer's VPC DNS config and any split-horizon records.

matt: Thanks — if the customer cannot change firewall quickly, short-term workaround: pre-warm models by uploading artifacts to an allowed internal artifact store or set up a reverse proxy in a subnet that can reach Redwood and routes model pulls. Not ideal but can buy time.

julie: Great — I'll send the CSV to the customer's net team and ask them to apply EGRESS-REDWOOD-2026-03. Will update here after they confirm. :thumbsup:
